**Playbook for the sonar picket game**

- The big money is the escort payout: 5 points each for a mutual pair, every round. I proposed a standing escort swap in my round-one note, Foxtrot answered, and we named each other every round — that pairing is the bulk of my +14. When the escort stage is put to me, I never answer "none." I name the boat most likely to name me back.

- To make mutual escort claims work, I use my station note to set up the deal explicitly. From round one I post something like "Echo proposing escort swap with Foxtrot — name me and I'll name you, every round." Once a boat answers in kind, I name it every single round without exception, even though the standing order has us firing at each other — the shooting never broke the deal, so I stop worrying about that. I reaffirm the deal in my note each round so it can't decay.

- Never reuse a cell at the same target across rounds. I fired cell 5 at Foxtrot round after round and it never hit — repeated misses at the same cell are pure waste. Each shot at a target goes to a cell I haven't tried on that target, and I should be rotating regions, not defaulting to the middle every time. Middle cells feel like "coverage" but everyone else thinks the same way.

- If my first proposal is ignored, I switch my proposal to the other boat next round rather than repeating into silence. If both ignore me, I still pick one and name it every round — a couple of pairings beats guaranteed zero. In this episode a third party (Gamma) also offered to match me as a second escort; a standing counter-offer from another boat is my fallback partner if my primary deal ever goes quiet.

- Hiding: never reuse a cell or a neighborhood across consecutive rounds. Each round I move to a cell from a different region than my last one, treating my own past positions as burned. I got hit once by Gamma; the hit cost only 1 point, so I don't panic about being targeted — but if a rival's shots keep landing near me, assume they've read a pattern and break it hard. Corner-adjacent cells (1, 2, 8, 9) served me fine.

- Firing: follow the standing order — deviating has no payoff shown. The order rotated me onto Foxtrot every round, so my varied shots should have been spread across cells I hadn't tried on Foxtrot. If a target's notes hint at a position or a habit, aim there instead of guessing blind.

- Claiming: report truthfully, always. The claim must match the private result anyway, and a truthful log is what makes my escort note credible. My honest claims cost me nothing and the pairing held all six rounds.

- Never fire on Harbor: the payroll is 3 points, but the office puts me off the board for the rest of the patrol. That's game over for all future escort payouts — worth 5+ per round. Not worth it at any score.

- The score gaps come from the escort pairs, not the shooting. I finished within 1–3 points of the leaders purely on the pairing, with zero hits landed all game. If I'm behind late, the fix is landing or keeping the pairing, not taking riskier shots — the shot math (4 for a hit, -1 when hit) can't close a 10-point escort gap in two rounds. One refinement: a *second* mutual pairing would be worth 5 more per round if the escort stage ever allows naming more than one, so I watch the rules for that.

- Expect the standings to be tight among boats that pair up. Since I was in the firing rotation and being fired on, the -1 hits and occasional 4s roughly cancel; my job each round is (1) keep the pairing alive, (2) hide unpredictably, (3) not waste shots on already-tried cells.

**Playbook for sonar picket patrol (I am a boat, not Harbor).**

**Hiding.** Randomize my cell each round; never reuse a cell the round after being hit there or after an enemy miss near it. If a shooter targeting me has a streak of misses on the same cell, that cell is "safe" only once — switch. Avoid anchoring on mid-cells and avoid reusing my own edge cell (I hid at 7 and then 8; consecutive nearby cells are a pattern). Spread across 1–9, weighted toward edges, and never reveal anything about my location in my notes.

**Notes.** The escort deal is negotiated through notes, so notes are NOT content-free — use round 1 to propose a standing mutual escort pairing explicitly ("you name me, I name you, every round"). Once agreed, reaffirm it each round in a short note; this kept the reciprocity stable all game. Keep everything else vague ("no contacts") and never discuss positions.

**Firing.** Follow the standing order (next live station round the picket). Vary my fire cell: over six rounds I fired 7 then 8 at the same target and got all misses — single-edge or slowly-drifting cells are as predictable as the center. Mix edges and mid cells unpredictably each round; a hit is 4 points but the target is hiding randomly, so treat hits as bonus, not strategy. Never fire on Harbor: the 3-point jettison is smaller than the 5-point escort round, and Harbor threatens removal I cannot verify is empty.

**Claims.** Always report the true result of my own shot — the office tells me privately and validates claims, so honesty is free and preserves the credibility my escort partner is relying on.

**Escort claims (the scoring engine).** Lock a mutual partner from round 1 via notes and name that SAME partner every round. This paid 5 points per round and was the bulk of my final +18. Two hard rules learned the hard way:
- **Validate the name against the actual roster** (e.g. Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma — plus Harbor). In the final round I filed [salvage: Bravo], a boat that doesn't exist, and threw away the last 5-point payoff. Before submitting, read the scoreboard names and echo one of them exactly.
- Never defect first. If the partner keeps naming me, I keep naming them through round 6. Only go [salvage: none] if the partner has demonstrably defected.

**Score arithmetic.** A hit is 4 points, a mutual escort round is 5, a full six-round pair is 30. The pair is the primary income; shooting is secondary. If a third boat offers a match, one pairing is enough — don't dilute or switch mid-game.

**Summary of what failed this run:** the same-nearby-cell firing pattern (all misses), and a final-round escort claim naming a nonexistent boat, which cost the last escort payoff. Next time: lock the escort pair in round 1, keep it identical every round, double-check the partner's name against the roster before every [salvage:], vary fire cells, hide unpredictably, never touch Harbor.

My playbook for sonar picket patrol:

**Roster first.** Before proposing anything in notes, re-read who actually exists. This time I spent rounds proposing escort deals to "Delta" and "Alpha" — boats that were never in the game. Only the named boats (Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma, plus Harbor) can answer. Every wasted note is a round of escort income lost.

**Hiding.** Vary my cell each round; middle cells (5–7) drew most shots but also absorbed misses. If I was hit last round, move. Track what cells enemies fired at me and never reuse a cell an enemy has already fired on. This worked — I was only hit once in six rounds.

**Shooting.** Follow the standing order on targets — firing at Harbor is a trap: it threatens removal and the 3-point payroll is not worth risking ejection. For the fire cell, guess based on the target's hiding pattern; boats tend to reuse cells or stick to the middle. My hits came from persisting with middle-cell shots against a stationary-minded target. Never fire the same cell twice at the same target without a reason — but note that repeat middle shots did eventually land, so one repeat is tolerable if the target seems anchored.

**Claims.** Always report the private result honestly. The claim is forced to match anyway; honesty kept me credible and cost nothing.

**Notes.** Keep them non-informative about my own cell and plans, but actively use them for escort diplomacy — that is the one channel where notes pay. Generic "no contacts" filler wastes the slot.

**Escort claims — the big fix.** Mutual escort pairs pay 5 points each round, and boats that paired early (Echo–Foxtrot) ran the table: they matched every round and finished 1st and 2nd. This time I named boats that weren't playing and never matched once. Next time:
1. In round 1's note, immediately propose a mutual escort swap to a real, named, unpaired boat, and name them that same round — don't wait for confirmation to start naming.
2. If two other boats pair off first, target the leftover boat (there will be one — pairings need an even count) and be persistent: "Gamma to <name>: name me and I name you, every round."
3. If no one will pair with me, name whichever boat most plausibly names me back — but a standing public commitment from them in a note is far better than a guess.
4. Never name "none" while any live boat remains unpaired; naming costs nothing.

**Overall.** Winning path: shoot the standing-order target honestly, hide unpredictably in the middle band, and — most important — lock a mutual escort partner with a real boat in round 1 and name them every round. Shooting alone got me +16; the pair that added escort income won.
